title: Two different faces
stem: A fair tetrahedral die has faces numbered 1 to 4. It is rolled twice. A technician records the larger score, using the common score if there is a tie.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Find the probability that the score recorded is 3.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: In 256 independent trials, give the expected number recording 3. A student predicts exactly this many. Comment.

steps.text: There are 16 equally likely ordered outcomes.
Count outcomes with both values at most 3 and subtract those with both at most 2.
Multiply the event probability by 256.
The expectation is 80.
Actual counts vary between runs. An expectation is a long-run average.

title: A fair simulation from digits
stem: A simulator produces independent random digits 0–9 with equal probabilities. A game needs three equally likely colours. Lin assigns 0–3 to red, 4–6 to blue and 7–9 to green.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Calculate the probability of two reds in the first two colours under Lin’s rule. Compare with a fair game.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Design a colour rule using the same generator that gives three equally likely colours. Justify it.

parts.label: c
parts.prompt: For your rule using one discarded digit, find the probability that at least one redraw is required while producing the first four colours.

steps.text: Use independence to square the probability of red.
Lin gives 0.16, whereas fairness gives $1/9$.
Assign three digits apiece, for example 0–2, 3–5 and 6–8.
Discard 9 and draw again.
Conditional on acceptance each group has probability $3/9$.
Use the complement of four immediate acceptances.

title: A second check on a parcel
stem: At a sorting depot, 12% of parcels need relabelling. A scanner flags 85% of those needing relabelling and 5% of all other parcels. A random parcel is selected.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Find the probability it is flagged.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Given that it is flagged, find the probability it needs relabelling. Explain why the answer differs from 0.85.

parts.label: c
parts.prompt: The false-flag rate is adjustable. Find the largest false-flag rate for which at least 80% of flagged parcels need relabelling, with other rates fixed.

steps.text: Add the two mutually exclusive routes to a flag.
The 85% is conditioned on a parcel needing relabelling. The group of flagged parcels also contains false alarms.
Rearrangement gives $0.0255≥0.88f$.
$f≤0.02898$ approximately, so at most 2.90% to three significant figures.

title: Two gates at a venue
stem: At a concert, 120 people used the east gate and 80 the west gate during a recorded interval. Of these, 18 east-gate and 4 west-gate visitors waited more than five minutes.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Estimate the probability of a long wait for a randomly selected visitor in that interval.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: On another evening 40% use the east gate. Assuming the gate-specific rates stay the same, estimate the number of long waits among 600 visitors.

parts.label: c
parts.prompt: A manager attributes any change from 11% solely to faster service. Evaluate that conclusion.

steps.text: Pool the counts of long waits and visitors.
Weight 0.15 and 0.05 by 0.4 and 0.6.
The probability is 0.09.
Expect 54 visitors.
The mix of gates changed.
With both gate-specific wait rates unchanged the overall estimate still falls by two percentage points.
